summary: New-hire onboarding: data-visualization console access stuck due to identity crosswalk mapping mismatch
description: Issue summary: A recently hired PM cannot access the internal DataViz console after completing SSO and SCIM provisioning. The user record appears in Okta and SCIM logs, but the console returns 403 with a message 'no roles assigned'. Impact: New hire onboarding blocked (cannot run dashboards or join pairing session). This is delaying a planned sync meeting tomorrow with the product team and is time-sensitive. Environment: Production (us-west), internal console behind identity-proxy, SCIM ingest pipeline v2.2.2. Steps to reproduce: 1) Invite new user via HR-provisioner -> Okta created profile. 2) Auto-provisioner runs SCIM PATCH to identity service. 3) User signs in via Okta SSO and is authenticated, but the console shows 403 and the support-runbook 'check-user-roles' returns empty role list. Observed logs: SCIM PATCH succeeded (200). Okta event shows user assigned to group "prod-dataviz-users". Identity-proxy log shows upstream call to authz service returned 204 NoContent. The console auth middleware logs: "role_lookup: 0 roles for subject=okta|12345-abcd". Hypothesis: crosswalk mapping between Okta group displayName and internal role key is failing due to a legacy transform that strips punctuation and lowercases; some groups created by IT include a trailing non-ASCII hyphen which is not normalized and therefore fails match in the role catalog.
steps_to_reproduce: Create Okta group with non-ASCII hyphen in displayName
Assign user to that Okta group
Allow SCIM provisioning to run and then attempt SSO login to console
logs: okta: event=group.assignment user=ava.test@redwood.com group=prod-dataviz\u2013team (note: U+2013 EN DASH present)
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:45 - Support triage: confirmed user exists in Okta and SCIM; console role lookup returned empty list
03/10 11:30 - Pulled role-catalog dump from authz-service; entries contain 'prod-dataviz-team' (ASCII hyphen) but not the en-dash variant
03/10 13:10 - Replayed provisioning PATCH locally with displayName normalized to ASCII hyphen; role mapping succeeded and console access granted in staging replay

03/11 08:20 - Reviewed transformation code in identity-proxy: uses python unicodedata.normalize('NFKC') but then strips '-' only for ASCII. Non-ASCII hyphen characters pass through unchanged, so lookup key does not match catalog.
comments: Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-10: Initial report from hiring manager — new PM cannot access DataViz; confirmed 403 with 'no roles assigned'

root_cause: Role mapping relies on exact-match keys derived from Okta group displayName. Some Okta groups created by IT contained non-ASCII dash-like characters (e.g., en-dash U+2013). The SCIM/provisioner and identity-proxy pipeline did not fully normalize these variants to the canonical ASCII hyphen, so lookup against the role catalog failed, returning no roles.
resolution: Temporary workaround: manually assign the 'dataviz-viewer' role to the affected user in the admin console (documented in the support note sent to the hiring manager). Permanent fix deployed: PR #1724 normalizes incoming group displayName by applying unicode NFKD normalization, mapping common dash-like characters (U+2013, U+2014, U+2212) to ASCII hyphen, then lowercasing and collapsing whitespace before performing role lookup. The fix was rolled out to identity-proxy and provisioner v2.2.3 on 2026-03-12 in us-west with canary at 10% then 100% after 30 minutes. Post-deploy verification: recreating the original user flow now yields correct role lookup and console access.
postmortem_follow_up: Add unit tests for dash-like character normalization in identity-proxy and scim-provisioner
Run a catalog-scan job to detect existing Okta groups with non-ASCII punctuation and create a remediation plan (automation or guided IT cleanup)
Add telemetry alert: spike in 'role_lookup: 0 roles' per new-user provisioning events to catch regressions
Document workaround and update onboarding runbook to include group name normalization guidance for IT
